samples.summary: The "writes nothing" test cannot distinguish the pre-update tab check from an in-update throw
samples.evidence: `worksheet-images.controller.ts` deliberately calls `this.worksheetOrThrow(doc.getRoot(), tabId)` *before* `doc.update`, with a comment saying an in-update throw "leaves an aborted change on a document this request should not have touched". The test at `worksheet-images.controller.spec.ts:92` ("404s an unknown tab and writes nothing") asserts only that the *other* tab's images are unchanged. Since the unknown tab ('nope') has no `sheets` entry, the assertion holds identically if the check were moved inside `doc.update` (the fake `update: (fn) => fn(root)` runs the callback and the throw propagates before any write to any tab). No test observes whether `doc.update` was entered, so the code shape the docblock justifies is uncovered.
searchedFor: grep for doc.update assertions in the spec

samples.summary: "keeps a concurrent edit to another slide" simulates no concurrency and compares a copy to itself
samples.evidence: The test takes `const peerEdit = { ...untouched.elements[0] }` *before* the operation and then asserts `expect(slides()[0].elements[0]).toEqual(peerEdit)` — comparing an object to a shallow copy of itself, which is true regardless of the implementation. No edit is applied between the read and the write, so the stated point ("only the one slide is written") rests solely on `expect(slides()[0]).toBe(untouched)`; a whole-array assignment that reused the same slide objects would also pass. The genuine lost-update case is only covered in `slide-ops.spec.ts` ('resolves the insertion point by source id'), not here.

samples.summary: No test for an orphaned sheet thread reporting `ref: null`
samples.evidence: `withSref` documents that the derived `ref` is `null` "once the row or column it pointed at is deleted — which is exactly how the editor tells an orphaned thread from a live one". `comments.controller.spec.ts` only asserts refs `['A1','B2']` for live anchors ('lists threads across every tab'); no test deletes/omits the anchored row or column id and checks the reported `ref`. A regression here (e.g. throwing, or reporting a stale ref) would silently mislead agents about whether a thread is still anchored.

samples.summary: None of the ~16 new HttpClient methods have their URL/verb/body asserted anywhere
samples.evidence: `class-b-commands.test.ts` mocks the entire `HttpClient` module (`vi.mock('../src/client/http-client.js', ...)`), so it only proves which client method a command reaches for. `http-client-paths.test.ts` was not extended and covers only pre-existing methods for escaping. Consequently `deleteTab`, `moveTab`, `duplicateTab`, `get/setWorksheetImages`, `listSlideLayouts`, `add/duplicate/move/deleteSlide`, `get/putBoardContent`, `listComments`, `createCommentThread`, `replyToComment`, `setCommentResolved`, `delete{CommentThread,Comment}` have no test asserting path, method or body. Only two paths are checked at all, via `printDryRun` in the command layer (tab duplicate, board set-content) — and those paths are re-built in the command, so a divergence between command preview and client request is invisible.

samples.summary: `planCommentNotifications` has no dedicated test despite the docblock claiming one; anonymous/non-numeric author paths uncovered
samples.evidence: The docblock says "Exported for its own test: this is the only part of the notification path that is a decision rather than a database write", but grep for `planCommentNotifications` across the repo finds it only in `comments.controller.ts`, the frontend's own `notify.ts`/`notify.test.ts` and a design doc — there is no backend spec importing it. Coverage exists only indirectly through the controller spec, which never exercises `toUserId` rejecting a non-numeric `CommentAuthor.userId` (the documented share-link/anonymous case) nor the `actorId === null` early return in `notify`, so a regression that started notifying (or crashing on) anonymous participants would pass.

`applyDelete` guards `if (root.sheets?.[tabId]) delete root.sheets[tabId]` specifically because "a `datasource` / `lakehouse` tab has metadata and no `sheets` entry". `tab-ops.spec.ts` only deletes a tab created via `createTab` (which always has a worksheet), and `tabs.controller.spec.ts` uses a datasource tab only for the *duplicate* 400 case. No test deletes a worksheet-less tab.
searchedFor: grep datasource in backend yorkie/api tests

samples.summary: `sheets images set` stdin path and its dry-run preview are untested
samples.evidence: `class-b-commands.test.ts` only drives `images set` with `--data`. The stdin branch (`for await (const chunk of process.stdin)`) and its distinct error message ("on stdin"), plus the destructive PUT dry-run preview (which is the only place the wire body `{ images: [...] }` unwrapping is observable), have no test. `images get` also has no dry-run test, unlike the tab/board commands in the same file.

samples.summary: No test asserts the new namespaces are actually mounted (sheets images, slides layouts/slide, top-level comments/board)
samples.evidence: `class-b-commands.test.ts` builds a throwaway program (`program.command('sheets')`, `registerSlidesEditCommand(program.command('slides'))`) rather than the real `registerSheetsCommand`/`registerSlidesCommand`/`buildProgram`, so it passes even if the registration lines in `sheets.ts`, `slides.ts` or `cli.ts` were removed. `namespaces.test.ts` does not check `images`, `layouts` or `slide` subcommands, and `output.test.ts:923` uses `expect.arrayContaining`, so `comments`/`board` are not required on the default program. Only `tabs.test.ts` was updated to assert its verb set.

samples.summary: Small uncovered branches in the comments controller: unknown-comment 404, missing `rect`, doc/pdf delete arm
samples.evidence: `deleteComment`'s `NotFoundException('Comment not found')` is never triggered from the controller (only `applyDeleteComment` returns `not_found` in the unit spec); `parsePdfAnchor`'s "'rect' must be an object" branch (rect omitted or non-object) has no test — only an out-of-range `w: 2`; and no test exercises `deleteThread`/`deleteComment` on the flat (`doc`/`pdf`) root arm of `mutateMap`, nor the `docKeyPrefix` used by `list` for a PDF.

samples.summary: `readBoardRoot` proxy-unwrapping is only tested for `elements`, not `meta`
samples.evidence: `readBoardRoot` calls `unwrapJson` on both `root.meta` and `root.elements`, but the spec's proxy test ('unwraps a Yorkie proxy through its own toJSON') only supplies a proxied `elements`. A `meta` proxy (which is what a real attached board root carries) is never exercised, so a spread-instead-of-unwrap regression on `meta` would pass.

finding.summary: No test at all for the new `board` arm of the content endpoint (GET dispatch, PUT dispatch, `assertValidBoardBody`, `sniffBodyShape` board branch)
finding.evidence: `docs-content.controller.spec.ts` tests GET/PUT per type for doc, slides and note (e.g. line 143 'returns the note content JSON…', line 270 'writes a note body via doc.update…', line 333 shape-vs-type mismatch), but a case-insensitive grep for 'board' across packages/backend/src/api/v1 returns zero matches. So the board `docKeyPrefix: 'board-'`, `initialBoardRoot()` seeding, the `elements`-after-`slides` sniff ordering, and every branch of the ~45-line `assertValidBoardBody` (meta.title, meta.unit, meta.recentColors, per-element walk) ship untested. `board-tree.spec.ts` only covers the read/write helpers in isolation, not the controller wiring or the validator. A wrong sniff order or a mis-dispatched write would overwrite board content through the wrong writer — data loss.

verdict.reason: The finding's key evidence claim (zero case-insensitive 'board' matches in packages/backend/src/api/v1) is factually wrong. docs-content.controller.spec.ts has a dedicated `describe('board')` suite at lines 1593-1757 covering every item the finding lists as untested: GET dispatch asserting docKeyPrefix 'board-' + syncMode readonly (1614-1632, vs controller 139-145); PUT dispatch asserting the captured root received meta/elements from writeBoardRoot and that opts.docKeyPrefix==='board-' and opts.initialRoot equals initialBoardRoot()'s `{meta:{title:'Untitled board'},elements:[]}` (1634-1668, vs controller 222-232); the sniff ordering — a full slides fixture PUT at a board-typed doc must yield "shape 'slides' ... type 'board'" (1670-1684), which is exactly the mis-dispatch/data-loss case, plus the mirror board-body-to-slides-doc case (1686-1699); and assertValidBoardBody's branches: missing meta (1711), blank meta.title (1715), bad meta.unit (1722), non-string meta.recentColors (1729), the shared per-element walk rejecting a missing `frame` (1736) and a missing `id` (1748) with the metadata lookup asserted not to have run. The assertions are substantive (captured CRDT root state and the concrete options object), not mock-call-only, so a wrong prefix, missing initialRoot, or reversed sniff order would fail them.

finding.summary: New destructive PUT/GET worksheet-images controller has no spec; only the pure `parseImages` validator is tested
finding.evidence: `worksheet-images.spec.ts` covers `parseImages` thoroughly, but there is no `worksheet-images.controller.spec.ts` (glob of packages/backend/src/api/v1/*.spec.ts lists every sibling controller — tabs, charts, rules, styles, dimensions — but not this one). Untested controller behavior: `setImages` wipes `ws.images = {}` and rekeys by id (an omitted image is deleted — data loss if the rekeying or the tab lookup is wrong), the `worksheetOrThrow` NotFoundException thrown *inside* `doc.update`, the sheet-type guard, and `getImages`' `unwrapJson` detach path which the code comment says is what keeps `res.json()` from blowing up on a Yorkie proxy.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing spec exists: packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-images.controller.spec.ts is a 159-line controller spec that exercises exactly the behaviors the finding lists as untested. It covers the destructive PUT replace (spec:72-81 asserts an omitted image is deleted; spec:83-87 asserts an empty list clears the collection), id-rekeying (spec:59-70 asserting Object.keys of root.sheets[TAB].images and the round-tripped anchor), the tab NotFoundException plus non-mutation of the existing tab (spec:89-96), the sheet-type BadRequest guard with withDocument never called (spec:105-115), the malformed-payload gate (spec:98-103), and getImages' unwrapJson detach path via a Yorkie-style proxy whose toJSON returns a JSON string (spec:127-144) plus syncMode readonly. The tests run against a real createSpreadsheetDocument() root with only YorkieService/DocumentService stubbed, so the logic under test is not mocked away and the assertions would fail if rekeying, tab lookup, guard, or unwrap broke. Jest collects the file (packages/backend/package.json:110 testRegex ".*\\.spec\\.ts$"). The finding also misdescribes the code: the tab check happens before doc.update (controller.ts:104-106), not inside it.

finding.summary: New tab delete/move/duplicate endpoints are untested at the controller level, including the `unwrapJson` proxy-detach the duplicate handler exists to do
finding.evidence: `tabs.controller.spec.ts` describes only 'ApiV1TabsController create/rename' (lines 13–160): create, rename, non-sheet documents, initialRoot seeding. Nothing exercises `remove`, `move` or `duplicate`. `tab-ops.spec.ts` covers the pure resolvers/appliers with plain objects, so what remains untested is exactly the controller-only logic: the 404/409 mapping (last_tab, pivot_dependents message listing dependents), and `duplicate`'s `unwrapJson(root.sheets?.[tabId])` — whose own comment says that without it Yorkie's `toJSON` string is stored instead of a grid, i.e. a silently corrupted duplicated tab.

verdict.reason: The spec file contains a second top-level suite the reviewer missed. tabs.controller.spec.ts:169 opens describe('ApiV1TabsController delete/move/duplicate'), running to line 365, and it covers precisely the behaviors claimed untested: remove happy path plus 404, 409 last_tab, and 409 pivot_dependents asserting the message names the dependent tab (lines 205-241); move reorder/clamp/400-validation/404 (257-288); and duplicate including a dedicated test 'detaches the source worksheet through the proxy's own toJSON' (309-326) that installs a toJSON-bearing proxy on root.sheets['tab-1'] and asserts the duplicate is stored as an object with parsed cells rather than Yorkie's JSON string — the exact unwrapJson behavior (tabs.controller.ts:249, yorkie-json.ts:14-30) the finding says nothing exercises. A further test (328-341) covers the unescaped-control-character repair path in parseJsonSnapshot (yorkie-json.ts:109-121). The tests are not over-mocked: the fake doc's getRoot/update mutate a real createSpreadsheetDocument() root (184-202), so the controller plus real tab-ops and unwrapJson execute; deleting the unwrapJson call would fail the assertion at 324-325. The finding's quoted evidence ('describes only ... lines 13-160') is contradicted by the file itself.

finding.summary: The test named 'lists threads across every tab' uses a single-tab fixture, so the cross-tab thread walk (`tabIdOfThread`, the `tabOrder` loop in `list`) is never exercised
finding.evidence: `sheetRoot()` (spec line ~46) builds `createSpreadsheetDocument()` and only touches `sheets['tab-1']`; the test creates one thread on 'tab-1' and asserts `threads.map(t => t.id)` equals `[first.id]` — true whether or not the controller walks more than the first tab. Every other test (reply/resolve/delete) also runs against that one tab, so `tabIdOfThread` (comments.controller.ts:474) resolving a thread stored under a non-first tab is untested. That routing is the controller's central design claim ('the tab is not in the path — a thread id is unique across the document'); if it regressed, threads on any second tab would 404 on reply/resolve/delete and vanish from `list`.

verdict.reason: The fixture is two-tab, not single-tab, and the cross-tab walk is directly exercised. `sheetRoot()` (comments.controller.spec.ts:68-81) clones the default worksheet into `sheets['tab-2']`, adds `tabs['tab-2']` and pushes 'tab-2' onto `tabOrder`, materializing rowOrder/colOrder on both tabs; `createSpreadsheetDocument()` seeds only DEFAULT_TAB_ID='tab-1' (worksheet-document.ts:139,189-192), so 'tab-2' is genuinely a non-first tab. The test 'lists threads across every tab' (spec:140-163) creates a thread on tab-1 AND one on tab-2 (spec:149-154) and asserts ids [first,second], anchor.tabId ['tab-1','tab-2'] and refs ['A1','B2'] — all of which fail if the `tabOrder` loop in `list` (comments.controller.ts:218-224) stopped at the first tab. Separately, 'finds a thread on a non-first tab by id alone' (spec:165-200) creates a thread on tab-2 and exercises reply/setResolved/deleteThread by id only, which route through `tabIdOfThread` (comments.controller.ts:449-450, 705-714), asserting tab-1 comments stay empty and tab-2 holds then loses the thread. The harness (spec:26-61) executes getRoot/update against the real root, so the logic is not mocked away. The finding's quoted evidence does not match the file in this repository.
